modern:
Do not be carried along thoughtlessly by the appearance of things, but give help to all according to your ability and their fitness; and if they have suffered loss in matters which are indifferent, do not imagine this to be a harm; for it is a bad habit. But as the old man, when he went away, asked for his foster-child’s top back, remembering that it was a top, so you too should do in this case.

When you are calling out on the Rostra, have you forgotten, man, what these things are?—Yes; but they are objects of great concern to these people.—Will you too, then, be made a fool for these things? I was once a fortunate man, but I lost it, I don’t know how.—But fortunate means that a man has assigned to himself a good fortune: and a good fortune is a good disposition of the soul, good emotions, good actions.
original:
Do not be carried along inconsiderately by the appearance of things, but give help [to all] according to thy ability and their fitness; and if they should have sustained loss in matters which are indifferent, do not imagine this to be a damage; for it is a bad habit. But as the old man, when he went away, asked back his foster-child’s top, remembering that it was a top, so do thou in this case also.

When thou art calling out on the Rostra, hast thou forgotten, man, what these things are?—Yes; but they are objects of great concern to these people—wilt thou too then be made a fool for these things? I was once a fortunate man, but I lost it, I know not how.—But fortunate means that a man has assigned to himself a good fortune: and a good fortune is good disposition of the soul, good emotions, good actions.

explained.summary:
Don’t get swept away by how things look. Help people as far as you can and as far as they need, but when they lose things that aren’t truly good or bad, such as money or position, don’t treat it as a real harm. That’s a bad habit. Marcus offers the image of an old man asking for his foster-child’s spinning top back, knowing all along it’s only a toy: you can go along with someone’s loss while seeing it clearly.

The ending is fragmentary. Someone shouting from a public platform forgets what such things are worth, and a man who says he lost his good fortune is told that real good fortune is a good character, good feelings and good actions.
explained.today: When a friend is gutted about a dent in their car or a missed promotion, you can sympathise and help without agreeing that their life is ruined. Real good luck is being the kind of person who stays decent whatever happens to the car.
